verdict.rationale: Daily's dial-in/dial-out docs say it is tested with multiple CPaaS vendors (Twilio, Telnyx, SignalWire) and SIP hardware phones, and that it accepts DTMF from SIP callers. That shows SIP interoperability that is not tied to one carrier. However, the evidence never documents how to connect your own SIP trunk (configuration, endpoints, authentication), so the depth of bring-your-own-carrier support is unproven. Missing for 10: documented BYO SIP trunk setup and configuration, explicit statement that existing carrier trunks can be used without Daily numbers, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, the service documents SIP interoperability with my existing trunking or telephony provider rather than locking me to one carrier

citations.quote: Tested with CPaaS vendors (Twilio, Telnyx, SignalWire) and SIP hardware phones (Poly, Cisco).
Daily can receive DTMF from a PSTN or SIP caller and deliver it to the room.
incoming calls trigger a webhook where you can define logic to route the call to a Daily room without requiring a PIN.
